papers.title: No-Touch vs Conventional Vein Grafts in Coronary Surgery: Seven-Year Clinical Outcomes of the SWEDEGRAFT Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.summary: Prespecified seven-year follow-up of SWEDEGRAFT, randomising 900 patients after coronary bypass to no-touch or conventional saphenous vein harvesting. Death, myocardial infarction or repeat revascularisation occurred in 19.8% versus 20.4% (hazard ratio 0.98). With previously reported excess leg-wound complications, routine no-touch harvesting lacked a net clinical benefit.
papers.short_title: seven-year SWEDEGRAFT outcomes of no-touch vein grafts in coronary surgery

papers.title: Cardiovascular safety of orforglipron versus insulin glargine in adults with type 2 diabetes and increased cardiovascular risk.
papers.summary: Phase 3 randomised trial of oral orforglipron versus insulin glargine in 2,749 adults with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk. Over a median two years, four-component major adverse cardiovascular events occurred in 4.2% versus 5.0% (hazard ratio 0.84), meeting non-inferiority. Gastrointestinal events were more common and hypoglycaemia less common with orforglipron.
papers.short_title: cardiovascular safety of oral orforglipron versus insulin glargine

papers.title: Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Overlap in Patients Hospitalized for Heart Failure.
papers.summary: In Get With The Guidelines–Heart Failure, among 725,205 US patients hospitalised for heart failure, 71.9% had two or more overlapping cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic conditions. More conditions meant stepwise higher in-hospital death and, in Medicare beneficiaries, higher one-year mortality and heart-failure readmission, with the strongest associations in reduced ejection fraction.
papers.short_title: cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic overlap in hospitalised heart failure

papers.title: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Heart Failure, 1990-2023: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
papers.summary: Global Burden of Disease estimates put heart failure at 56.0 million cases worldwide in 2023. Ischaemic and hypertensive heart disease dominated in older adults, while congenital disease, rheumatic heart disease, alcohol and Chagas varied by age and region. Most aetiologies are preventable through blood pressure, alcohol and tobacco control.
papers.short_title: the global burden of heart failure from 1990 to 2023

papers.title: Food and Health: Nutrition for Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement: A Report of the American College of Cardiology.
papers.summary: This American College of Cardiology scientific statement reviews nutrition for cardiovascular disease prevention and management. Evidence supports replacing saturated with unsaturated fats, more fibre and whole grains, less sodium and ultra-processed foods, and Mediterranean, DASH or plant-rich patterns. It urges dietary counselling, Food Is Medicine programmes and clinician education in practice.
papers.short_title: the 2026 ACC scientific statement on nutrition and cardiovascular disease
